upoaa.note: Durable Power of Attorney Act (Est. Code ch. 751-752) has a uniformity clause and UPOAA-like acceptance, reliance and termination rules added in 2017 (HB 1974), but it is not titled UPOAA and does not make POAs durable by default. ULC enactment status not checked.

upc.note: Texas Estates Code, with independent administration and muniment of title.

rufadaa.note: Titled the 'Texas Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act' (2017), with Texas modifications such as §2001.051(c).

localNames: agent under statutory durable power of attorney

assigned.event: Adult principal signs a writing with durability words and acknowledges it before a notary or other authorized officer

starts.event: Immediately unless the principal selects 'effective upon my disability or incapacity'

ends.event: Principal revokes; POA's own termination terms; purpose accomplished; no agent remains
Permanent guardian of the estate qualifies (automatic revocation unless court orders suspension)

transitions.event: Temporary guardian of the estate qualifies
conditions: Unless court order affirms the POA and confirms the agent

transitions.event: Permanent guardian of the estate qualifies
conditions: Unless court orders suspension during guardianship
Agent must deliver assets and account to guardian

patches.diff: Texas requires notarial acknowledgment and express durability words (§751.0021), so Texas POAs are not durable by default as they are under UPOAA. A permanent guardian of the estate who qualifies automatically REVOKES the POA, and a temporary guardian SUSPENDS it (§751.133). Chapter 751 took on many UPOAA-style provisions in 2017 (HB 1974), including a uniformity clause (§751.003).

The Durable Power of Attorney Act covers only durable POAs (§751.0015). This research found no Texas statute governing when a nondurable POA starts or ends; presumably common-law agency applies (not verified).

localNames: power of attorney effective on disability or incapacity

starts.event: Principal's disability or incapacity; unless the POA defines it, a physician certifies in writing, after execution and based on a medical examination, that the principal cannot manage financial affairs

transitions.event: Physician's written certification of mental incapacity to manage financial affairs
conditions: POA may supply its own definition

patches.diff: Springing POAs rest on the statutory durability wording 'becomes effective on the disability or incapacity of the principal' (§751.0021(a)(3)(A)(ii)); §751.0021 has no separate springing provision. The default trigger is a physician's certification only (§751.00201), with no psychologist, attorney or judge option as under UPOAA.

localNames: agent under medical power of attorney

starts.event: Attending physician certifies in writing, filed in the medical record, that the principal is incompetent

ends.event: Revocation by oral or written notice or any act showing intent to revoke, regardless of principal's competence; or a later medical POA
Divorce, annulment or voiding of marriage to agent unless POA provides otherwise
Probate court suspends or revokes agent in guardianship proceeding

ends.note: Subchapter D does not state death as a termination event in the sections reviewed. Post-death control of remains needs a separate §711.002 appointment.

transitions.event: Principal objects to treatment decision
conditions: Treatment may not be given or withheld over the principal's objection, whether or not competent

transitions.event: Guardianship petition filed: court determines whether to suspend/revoke agent; if guardian appointed, guardian has sole authority pending determination

patches.diff: The trigger is narrower than UHCDA's: authority exists only after the attending physician certifies incompetence in writing in the medical record (§166.152(b)). The principal can revoke at any time regardless of mental state (§166.155(a)(1)), and treatment may not be given or withheld over the principal's objection. The medical POA is excluded from the Durable POA Act (§751.0015).

localNames: surrogate decision-maker (Consent to Medical Treatment Act)

assigned.event: Adult patient in hospital, nursing home, home health agency or county/municipal jail is comatose, incapacitated or unable to communicate, with no guardian or medical POA agent reasonably available

starts.event: Attending physician documents incapacity and proposed treatment and makes diligent effort to contact surrogates

transitions.event: Surrogate consents in priority order: spouse, adult children, parents, nearest living relative
conditions: Cannot consent to voluntary inpatient mental health services, electro-convulsive treatment, or appoint another surrogate
If none available, another uninvolved physician may concur

transitions.event: Life-sustaining treatment decision without directive: attending physician plus guardian/agent, or one person from spouse, adult children, parents, nearest relative
conditions: If no guardian and no listed person, second physician or ethics committee concurrence required

transitions.event: For jail inmates, surrogate authority expires at the earlier of 120 days or release

patches.diff: Texas has two default-surrogate statutes. Ch. 313 covers general medical treatment in listed settings but excludes life-sustaining treatment decisions, and §166.039 covers those decisions. The priority lists are shorter than UHCDA's (no siblings or close friends), and a disinterested physician's concurrence is the fallback. Disputes go to a court with Title 3 guardianship jurisdiction.

assigned.event: Court finds by clear and convincing evidence that the proposed ward is incapacitated and that alternatives and supports are not feasible

starts.event: Guardian qualifies (oath/declaration, bond if required) and clerk issues certificate as letters

ends.event: Ward dies (guardianship settled and closed; guardian may make funeral arrangements with court approval before closing)
Court finds full capacity, or sufficient capacity with supports and services

transitions.event: Letters expire 1 year 4 months after issuance unless renewed
Temporary guardian appointed on substantial evidence of incapacity and probable cause of immediate need; max 60 days except as §1251.052 provides
Qualification of a guardian terminates any supported decision-making agreement

patches.diff: Texas uses 'guardian' for adults (Estates Code Title 3). The court must find that alternatives, including supported decision-making agreements (ch. 1357), are not feasible. Letters expire after 16 months unless renewed (§1106.002). Termination at death is in §1202.001(b)(1); ch. 1204 covers final settlement, accounting and discharge.

assigned.event: Court appoints guardian of the estate after findings

ends.event: Ward's death triggers settlement; guardian presents final account; personal representative may compel account
Restoration to capacity, estate exhausted, or no longer necessary

transitions.event: Permanent guardian of estate qualifies; agent's powers under durable POA automatically revoked
Court grants guardian access to ward's digital assets after opportunity for hearing

patches.diff: Texas calls this role a 'guardian of the estate'. When a permanent guardian qualifies, the durable POA is revoked by operation of law (§751.133).

assigned.event: Named in will; application filed and will admitted to probate

starts.event: Executor qualifies (oath/declaration; bond if required) and clerk issues letters

ends.event: Independent administration closes 30 days after closing report or notice of closing (absent objection), terminating authority and cancelling letters

transitions.event: Fourth anniversary of death passes: will may not be admitted (absent proof applicant not in default) and letters testamentary may not issue unless application filed within 4 years
Will admitted as muniment of title (no unpaid debts other than real-estate liens, or no necessity); no executor is appointed
Named executor fails to qualify within 20 days after probate, or fails to present will within 30 days after death without good cause; administration with will annexed may be granted
Will directs independent administration; court involvement limited to probate, inventory and claims list

patches.diff: Texas has a 4-year deadline both to probate a will and to obtain letters testamentary (§§256.003, 301.002; the UPC's comparable limit is 3 years). Texas also offers muniment of title (ch. 257), which transfers property under the will with no personal representative, and independent administration that closes by filing a closing report or notice.

assigned.event: Court grants administration by priority (spouse, principal devisee, devisee, next of kin, creditor, ...) only if a necessity for administration exists

transitions.event: Court finds necessity (e.g., two or more debts, partition, recover property, dangerous real property)

patches.diff: Texas requires the court to find a necessity for administration (§306.002(b)-(c)) and applies the same 4-year filing limit (§301.002). A 'person designated as administrator' under §254.006 ranks just after the named executor (§304.001(a)(1-a)).

assigned.event: All capable distributees and two disinterested witnesses swear to affidavit listing assets, liabilities and heirship facts

starts.event: Decedent died intestate, 30 days have elapsed, no PR petition pending or granted, non-exempt assets (excluding homestead and exempt property) do not exceed $75,000, and the judge approves the filed affidavit

ends.event: Assets delivered; distributees remain accountable to later-appointed PR and to persons with prior rights

transitions.event: If homestead is the only real property, title may pass under recorded affidavit

patches.diff: The Texas affidavit is available only for INTESTATE estates (§205.001). It must be filed with and approved by the court, requires two disinterested witnesses, waits 30 days, and caps non-exempt assets at $75,000. For testate small estates, muniment of title (ch. 257) is the usual route.

assigned.event: Selected by method in trust instrument; otherwise court appoints on petition

starts.event: Death, resignation, incapacity or removal of sole or surviving trustee

patches.diff: The Texas Trust Code (Prop. Code Title 9) is not the UTC. A trust is revocable unless it is irrevocable by its express terms (§112.051). No Texas analog to California's 60-day post-death trustee notice was identified in this research.

assigned.event: User directs custodian via online tool

patches.diff: Texas modified RUFADAA's override rule: a user's direction overrides only a terms-of-service provision that does not require the user to act affirmatively and separately from accepting the terms of service (§2001.051(c)).

starts.event: Written request plus death certificate and letters, §205.001 small estate affidavit, or other court order

transitions.event: PR obtains content of communications
conditions: Deceased user consented or a court directs

transitions.event: Agent obtains content where POA expressly grants that authority
Court grants guardian access after opportunity for hearing; guardian may request suspension/termination for good cause

patches.diff: Texas enacted RUFADAA in 2017 as Est. Code ch. 2001, with a guardian in place of the uniform act's conservator (§2001.171). The small estate affidavit filed under §205.001 is an accepted credential.

starts.event: At death, as first-priority class if agent could have made the gift immediately before death

patches.diff: Texas enacted the Revised UAGA (H&S ch. 692A). The §692A.009 priority list includes the hospital administrator as a separate class ahead of any other person with authority to dispose of the body.

patches.name: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: agent under Appointment for Disposition of Remains
patches.summary: The person who controls disposition of remains, including cremation, and must inter them. That person is liable for the reasonable cost of interment (except an executor or administrator) and may seek reimbursement from the estate.

assigned.event: Decedent signs a written instrument (statutory form available) with acknowledged signature naming agent and successors

starts.event: Decedent's death; agent must sign acceptance before acting

ends.event: Holder fails to make or delegate arrangements by the earlier of the 6th day after notice of death or the 10th day after death; right passes

ends.note: No explicit statutory end point; inferred.

transitions.event: Death: right vests by priority
conditions: (1) person designated in signed written instrument; (2) surviving spouse; (3) any one adult child; (4) either parent; (5) any one adult sibling; (6) qualified executor/administrator; (7) next of kin by inheritance order
DD Form 93 controls for certain military deaths

transitions.event: No arrangements by earlier of 6th day after notice or 10th day after death: presumed unable/unwilling; right passes
Divorce, annulment or voiding of marriage to spouse-agent before death revokes designation unless instrument provides otherwise

patches.diff: New role. Texas has a dedicated Appointment for Disposition of Remains form, separate from the medical POA. It must be acknowledged, and the agent must sign an acceptance before acting (§711.002(b)-(c)). The time limit for acting is short (6 days after notice or 10 days after death). An executor or administrator ranks 6th and is not personally liable for costs.
